clue.text: Bay's home, standing firm

blocks.note: first meaning: where a bay, a reddish-brown horse, is kept
second meaning: steady, not likely to give way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' suggests a stretch of coast, but here it is a horse of reddish-brown colour, whose home is a building for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse lives in a stable building, and anything steady and secure is described with the same adjective.

clue.text: Range small, not large – pick!

indicators.note: saying a word comes without something tells you to strike that letter out

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
a pick is the small plate used to pluck guitar strings
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone choosing from a range of sizes, told to take small rather than large.
explanation.walkthrough: S is followed by PLECTRUM with its L removed, giving SPECTRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full scale or span of possibilities, the same sense as a range of options.

clue.text: Perhaps Merkel's eaten 40% of icing that's used on cakes

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a noun: the thing that's used on cakes

indicators.note: a percentage of a five-letter word means keeping only two of its letters and cutting the rest
what has been eaten sits inside the eater, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Angela Merkel, the former German chancellor, is an example of someone with this first name
taken as written; only its first two letters survive the cut, since two of five is 40 per cent

explanation.surface: The German chancellor has helped herself to some of the cake icing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that Merkel is just one example of a woman with this first name; the definition is a description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelica is a plant whose candied green stems are a traditional decoration on cakes and trifles.

clue.text: Flower, gilt edges removed, clutched by gutted lady

indicators.note: taking off the edges leaves only the inner letters of a word
gutting removes the insides, leaving just the outside letters
something clutched is held tightly inside something else

blocks.note: the two inner letters once its outer ones go
only the first and last letters survive

explanation.surface: A golden-trimmed flower being gripped by a lady who has been badly let down.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'gilt' sits inside the outside of 'lady': L(IL)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The lily is a well-known garden plant with large trumpet-shaped blooms, so it is an example of a flower.

clue.text: Clots in kitchens, cooking

indicators.note: cooking transforms its ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Lumps forming in the sauce while people cook in their kitchens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clots' reads as a plural noun for lumps, or for fools in kitchens, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: When a liquid clots it becomes more solid and dense, which is what a sauce does as it sets.

clue.text: Old range destroyed in quiet stampede

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so these letters must be put back in a fresh order
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the eight letters, rearranged
hush means silence or quiet

explanation.surface: An old cattle range wrecked when the herd charges, a quiet moment turning into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old range' sounds like a cattle range from the frontier; the two words are anagram fodder, placed inside HUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a panicked, reckless dash by a crowd, exactly a hasty headlong charge forward.

clue.text: Smarty-pants, cold, the French musician, vacuous crook

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word loses all its inside letters

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
le is the French for 'the'
Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer
only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: A list of unflattering descriptions of some know-it-all: cold, foreign, a musician and an empty-headed criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first word; everything after it is a chain of small pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever dick is British slang for a show-off who parades their knowledge, the same scornful insult as smarty-pants.

clue.text: Setter had cryptic clue earlier: 'father of geometry?'

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscured, so these letters are disguised in a new order
coming earlier places this piece in front of the other

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
the setter is 'I', and 'I had' contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: The setter admits to having set a cryptic clue for a famous mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'setter' often means 'I'; so 'setter had' is I'D, which follows the rearranged CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek mathematician Euclid wrote the Elements and is traditionally called the founder of geometry.

clue.text: 'How do you spell "shy"?' That's pretty light stuff

indicators.note: spelling a word out means saying each of its letters one at a time

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
the second letter of the word
when you list letters aloud, the last two are joined by a conjunction
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A teacher asks a child to spell a word, then remarks on how easy that is.
explanation.walkthrough: Spelling the word out loud you say 'S, H and Y', and run together that gives the answer. A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beer diluted with lemonade, a shandy is a weak, low-alcohol drink, hence fairly light refreshment.

clue.text: Communist, English, ultimately smitten with posh ladies

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is wanted

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the last letter
gels is 'girls' as pronounced in an upper-class English accent

explanation.surface: A communist Englishman who in the end fell for some upper-class women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gels' is a jokey spelling of 'girls' in a plummy British accent, standard crossword shorthand for posh young women.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels co-wrote the Communist Manifesto with Marx, so he is a famous communist.

clue.text: Cave in, having consumed most of ale, in resort port on the Med

indicators.note: most but not all of a word means its last letter is dropped
what has been consumed is now inside the consumer
to re-sort something is to sort it again, putting letters in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: A tourist collapses after drinking too much beer at a Mediterranean holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday spot, but split as re-sort it tells you to rearrange CAVE IN with AL inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a major Spanish city with a large seaport on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Silly, stupid, bad: a fast scramble

indicators.note: something stupid is muddled and confused, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: these eight letters rearranged
to scramble is to hurry or rush

explanation.surface: A string of insults about something foolish, ending with a hurried mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupid' looks like part of a list of synonyms but signals the anagram; 'scramble' looks like a second anagram signal but is the hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft as a brush is a British idiom meaning extremely foolish or scatterbrained, a colourful way of saying silly.

clue.text: Up to cultivate the land

blocks.note: first meaning: until a certain time
second meaning: to plough and prepare soil for crops

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction to a farmer, but it splits into a preposition and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word serves both as a preposition meaning until and as a farming verb for ploughing soil.

clue.text: What moon reveals after autumn in Oregon Trail

indicators.note: coming after places one piece behind the other

blocks.note: fall is the American word for autumn
to moon someone is to show them your bare backside

explanation.surface: A view of the autumn moon rising over the Oregon Trail of pioneer days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moon' looks like the night-time satellite but is the verb for baring one's buttocks; 'Oregon Trail' looks like one name but the last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail is to lag at the back of a group or race, failing to keep up with others.

clue.text: Primarily modernized African democracy, although governor's a strongman called Andry Rajoelina?

definitions.text: African democracy, although governor's a strongman called Andry Rajoelina?
definitions.note: the whole clue describes the country

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is taken

blocks.clueFragment: modernized African democracy, although governor's a strongman called Andry Rajoelina
blocks.note: the initial letter of each of the ten words

explanation.surface: A sketch of an African nation that is nominally democratic yet led by a strongman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: its initial letters spell the answer, and it describes the island nation, whose president Andry Rajoelina first took power in a 2009 coup.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascar is an island republic off southeast Africa whose leader came to office through a military-backed takeover.

clue.text: With no humility, half of mum's brothers advanced

indicators.note: keeping only half a word means the other half is thrown away

blocks.note: your mother's brothers are your uncles
to advance something is to bring it forward or hurry it

explanation.surface: Arrogant relatives on the mother's side pushing themselves forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The first three letters of UNCLES are joined by HASTENED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unchastened has not been humbled or subdued by punishment or rebuke, so shows no meekness.

clue.text: Incomplete romantic gift Everyman had offered up in muddle

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing a part, here its final letter
in a down answer, sending letters up means reading them from bottom to top

blocks.note: a red rose is the classic token of love
the setter is 'I', and 'I had' contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A setter confesses to giving a half-hearted romantic present in a state of confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: RED ROSE loses its E, I'D is added, and the whole lot is turned upside down in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A muddle is a state of confusion or untidiness, which is exactly the sense of a disarray.

clue.text: Perhaps krypton might make you angriest?

indicators.note: these letters could be made into something else when rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Superman's home planet Krypton, and kryptonite, could make anyone furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Krypton' suggests Superman's planet, but here it is the chemical element; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Krypton is one of the noble elements, chemically unreactive gases such as neon and argon.

clue.text: Pulling muscles earlier in inattentive state

indicators.note: coming earlier means placed in front

blocks.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles
traction is the act of pulling or drawing along

explanation.surface: Someone who strained their muscles earlier while their mind was elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulling muscles' reads as an injury, but the two words are separate pieces, with the muscles placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstraction can mean absent-mindedness, being lost in thought and not noticing one's surroundings.

clue.text: Weatherman's line: 'I weep over a drop of rain'

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, just one letter from the start
in a down answer, being over something means sitting above it

blocks.note: taken as written
to sob is to cry or weep
taken as written
the first letter

explanation.surface: A TV forecaster's catchphrase lamenting the arrival of rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted words look like a forecaster's spoken line but are just the pieces, with 'Weatherman's line' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map, an isobar is a curve joining places of equal atmospheric pressure, drawn by forecasters.

clue.text: A little belligerent ombudsman in Bury

indicators.note: a little of something is a small portion, so only part of these words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A rather aggressive complaints official working in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is also a town near Manchester, which makes it look like a place rather than the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place a body in a tomb or grave, which is to inter or lay it to rest.

clue.text: 'Pudding!' announced by footballer in glad rags

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so we go by the sound rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a sundae is an ice-cream dessert
George Best, the famous Manchester United and Northern Ireland player

explanation.surface: A footballer in fancy clothes calls out for dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: Pudding is the British word for dessert. Only the first piece is sounded out; the footballer is spelt as is.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is slang for smart clothes kept for special occasions, traditionally the finest outfit worn to church.

clue.text: By sound of it, put up with a swine

indicators.note: going by how something sounds means listening rather than reading

blocks.note: to bear something is to put up with it; its past tense is bore

explanation.surface: Having to tolerate somebody who is a real pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' is past tense here: bore, the past of bear, which sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a male pig or a wild pig, and pigs are also called swine.

clue.text: Report of low reef in wharf

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so we go by sound

blocks.note: a key or cay is a low island or reef, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: News of a shallow reef found in the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: A key (from Spanish cayo) is a low coral island or reef.
explanation.definitionFit: A quay is a stone or concrete landing place where ships tie up, the same structure as a wharf.

clue.text: Arrest, finding weapon in bibliophiles' association

blocks.note: police book a suspect when charging them
a club is a heavy stick used as a weapon

explanation.surface: Police make an arrest after discovering a weapon at a reading group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finding' and 'in' link the pieces to the definition; there is no container here.
explanation.definitionFit: A bibliophile is a lover of books, and a society of such readers who meet to discuss them is a reading group.

clue.text: Trained gudong, one working with hunters

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so these letters are put into a new form

blocks.note: a nonsense word taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal, given an odd name, that has been trained to help on a shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is not a real word, which is a strong hint that it needs rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun dog such as a retriever or pointer is bred to find and fetch game for people shooting.

clue.text: Stir herb stews; they're regenerative

definitions.note: a clause describing a plural noun: things that are regenerative

indicators.note: stewing cooks things together into a mixture, so these letters are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Cooking instructions: stir herbs into restorative stews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'stews' does the job instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebirths are renewals or revivals, events which bring fresh life, which is what regeneration means.

clue.text: Fancy: 'Prussia' contains name of another country

indicators.note: a phrase that contains something holds it within its letters

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A historical musing that the old state of Prussia had another nation inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like the definition or an anagram signal, but it is only there for its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is an island republic in the eastern Mediterranean, a separate nation from the old German state.
